items.s: The magic show was ___! How did he do it?
items.tip: Two steps: believe → believable (drop the e, add -able), then un-: unbelievable.
items.say: The magic show was unbelievable! How did he do it?
items.ask: The magic show was blank! How did he do it?

items.s: Our trip to the beach was ___. We'll remember it for ever.
items.tip: un- + forget + -able; double the t: unforgettable (impossible to forget).
items.say: Our trip to the beach was unforgettable. We'll remember it for ever.
items.ask: Our trip to the beach was blank. We'll remember it for ever.

items.s: Much to our ___, the concert was cancelled.
items.tip: Two affixes: dis- + appoint + -ment. 'Much to our …' needs a noun.
items.say: Much to our disappointment, the concert was cancelled.
items.ask: Much to our blank, the concert was cancelled.

items.s: The weather in the mountains is very ___, so pack a raincoat.
items.tip: un- + predict + -able = unpredictable (you can't predict it).
items.say: The weather in the mountains is very unpredictable, so pack a raincoat.
items.ask: The weather in the mountains is very blank, so pack a raincoat.

items.s: The old camp bed was ___ hard, so I couldn't sleep.
items.tip: An adverb before hard: un- + comfortable, then -le → -ly: uncomfortably.
items.say: The old camp bed was uncomfortably hard, so I couldn't sleep.
items.ask: The old camp bed was blank hard, so I couldn't sleep.

items.s: The museum was ___ quiet on Monday morning.
items.tip: un- + expected + -ly: an adverb that describes quiet.
items.say: The museum was unexpectedly quiet on Monday morning.
items.ask: The museum was blank quiet on Monday morning.

items.s: Many countries celebrate their ___ Day with fireworks.
items.tip: in- (not) + depend + -ence: independence = not depending on others.
items.say: Many countries celebrate their independence Day with fireworks.
items.ask: Many countries celebrate their blank Day with fireworks.

items.s: The goats escaped because of his ___ with the gate.
items.tip: Stacked suffixes: care → careless (adjective) → carelessness (noun).
items.say: The goats escaped because of his carelessness with the gate.
items.ask: The goats escaped because of his blank with the gate.

items.s: Daily practice will ___ your muscles.
items.tip: will + verb. strong → strength (noun) → strengthen (-en = make): the o changes to e.
items.say: Daily practice will strengthen your muscles.
items.ask: Daily practice will blank your muscles.

items.s: They are going to ___ the road near our school.
items.tip: -en makes a verb meaning 'make more': wide → widen.
items.say: They are going to widen the road near our school.
items.ask: They are going to blank the road near our school.

items.s: Can you ___ the instructions? They're too hard for us.
items.tip: -ify = make: simple → simplify (the -le drops).
items.say: Can you simplify the instructions? They're too hard for us.
items.ask: Can you blank the instructions? They're too hard for us.

items.s: The museum wants to ___ its old dinosaur hall.
items.tip: -ise/-ize = make: modernise means make modern. Both spellings are right.
items.say: The museum wants to modernise its old dinosaur hall.
items.ask: The museum wants to blank its old dinosaur hall.

items.s: We used a special filter to ___ the pond water.
items.tip: pure → purify (drop the e, add -ify = make pure).
items.say: We used a special filter to purify the pond water.
items.ask: We used a special filter to blank the pond water.

items.s: Dark clouds ___ to spoil our picnic.
items.tip: threat (noun) → threaten (verb, -en). The sentence is in the past: threatened.
items.say: Dark clouds threatened to spoil our picnic.
items.ask: Dark clouds blank to spoil our picnic.

items.s: Scientists ___ animals into groups such as mammals and birds.
items.tip: class → classify (-ify = put into classes). They classify: no -s.
items.say: Scientists classify animals into groups such as mammals and birds.
items.ask: Scientists blank animals into groups such as mammals and birds.

items.s: The coach's kind words ___ me to try again.
items.tip: en- = give: encourage. Past tense: encouraged.
items.say: The coach's kind words encouraged me to try again.
items.ask: The coach's kind words blank me to try again.

items.s: Your ___ of new words is getting better and better.
items.tip: Watch the spelling: pronounce loses an o in the noun: pronunciation.
items.say: Your pronunciation of new words is getting better and better.
items.ask: Your blank of new words is getting better and better.

items.s: Thank you for your clear ___ of the rules.
items.tip: explain → explanation: the i disappears.
items.say: Thank you for your clear explanation of the rules.
items.ask: Thank you for your clear blank of the rules.

items.s: Everyone thanked the baker for his ___. He gave free cupcakes to the whole class.
items.tip: -ous → -osity: generous → generosity.
items.say: Everyone thanked the baker for his generosity. He gave free cupcakes to the whole class.
items.ask: Everyone thanked the baker for his blank. He gave free cupcakes to the whole class.

items.s: Learning a new song takes a lot of ___.
items.tip: repeat → repetition: the ea becomes e and we add -ition.
items.say: Learning a new song takes a lot of repetition.
items.ask: Learning a new song takes a lot of blank.

items.s: Sara is very ___. She got everyone to join the chess club.
items.tip: persuade → persuasive: the d changes to s.
items.say: Sara is very persuasive. She got everyone to join the chess club.
items.ask: Sara is very blank. She got everyone to join the chess club.

items.s: Write a short ___ of your favourite animal.
items.tip: describe → description: the b changes to p.
items.say: Write a short description of your favourite animal.
items.ask: Write a short blank of your favourite animal.

items.s: The ___ of the swimming pool is two metres.
items.tip: deep → depth: a noun that loses one e.
items.say: The depth of the swimming pool is two metres.
items.ask: The blank of the swimming pool is two metres.

items.s: Our old school bus needs regular ___.
items.tip: maintain → maintenance: the ai becomes e, then -ance.
items.say: Our old school bus needs regular maintenance.
items.ask: Our old school bus needs regular blank.
